details.goal: The two functions `trace` and `expand` are built on: resolve a free-text query into exactly one symbol (or an honest ambiguity), and expand one symbol's neighbourhood to a bounded depth with grouping.

tasks.title: domain: the git change set and freshness

details.goal: The only two modules that talk to git: the change set behind `summary(change)` and `impact`, and the staleness verdict every envelope's `read_status` reports.
steps: Port diff.rs's git runner and the name-status parser with the `-z` record split.
Port the rename-aware entry construction and the `degraded` path.
Port freshness.rs including the four HEAD shapes.
Write the tests against real temp git repositories created with `git init`.
details.verify:
`cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p sangkar-domain --test diff_freshness` exits 0 (git required; the test skips with a clear message if `git` is missing).
Done when: the rename case produces one entry with `state: renamed` and both paths, and the git-less directory produces `head_commit_of() == None` with `check_freshness` still answering.

progress.detail: diff.rs (1108 lines) ports diff.ts. Every git read is exactly `git --no-pager --no-optional-locks -c credential.helper= -c core.askpass= -C <root> <args>` with stdin null and piped output, and each invocation is bounded by a 5 ms `try_wait` poll loop against `GIT_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000` (`ChangedSinceOptions.git_timeout_ms` overrides) calling `Child::kill` (SIGKILL) at the deadline, with each pipe drained on its own thread so a full pipe cannot deadlock and a collection grace turning a held pipe into `degraded` rather than a hang; the `git diff` and `rev-parse --show-prefix` + `status --porcelain -z --untracked-files=all` reads run concurrently through `thread::scope`, so a hung git costs one budget (the TypeScript's `Promise.all`). `parse_name_status` splits the `-z` stream, takes the first character of `R100`/`C75` as the letter, requires both source and destination for R/C, skips a malformed record (truncated pair) without emptying the parse, and a rename produces ONE entry `{state: Renamed, path: destination, from: source}` — `git diff` keeps rename detection (`--no-renames` not passed; worker.ts's own flag untouched). `degraded` is set by a git failure (diff or status), the reason goes to `sangkar_core::log` rather than a `degradedReason` field the contract does not have; untracked paths pass the classify gate and become `state: Untracked` in `changed`+`entries`; `unmatched` carries the two TS reasons verbatim. `ChangeEntry.sha256` is the digest of the current working-tree bytes (None for deleted/unreadable), computed by a hand-rolled FIPS 180-4 `sha256_hex` (no dependency added; NIST vectors pinned in a unit test). freshness.rs (621 lines): `head_commit_of` reads `.git` (a directory or a `gitdir:` file), then HEAD's `ref:` → loose ref → `packed-refs`, and a raw sha for a detached HEAD, returning None (not an error) for a missing `.git` and never spawning a child; four shapes tested against real repos. Staleness source: `indexed_at = latest_generation().published_at` because `GraphMeta` deliberately has no timestamp and the newest publish by seq is the generation the read path serves, paired with `generation = meta.generation` (what a cursor binds to); documented in the module doc. The stall comparison parses `published_at` to epoch millis (`parse_iso8601_millis`, chosen over lexicographic compare because that cannot add the 600 000 ms budget) and fires only for `running`/`busy` with `now - published > WATCHER_STALL_MS = 600_000` (strict `>`, boundary pinned by a test at exactly 600 000 → fresh and 600 001 → stale). `STALE_REASONS` copied verbatim: ["none","files_changed","root_mismatch","base_commit_moved","watcher_stalled"]. Order: root_mismatch (only when `FreshnessOptions.repo_root` is supplied and differs from `meta.project_root`), files_changed_since count, base_commit_moved (case-insensitive prefix match of `generation.base_commit` against `head_commit_of` of the caller/recorded root), watcher_stalled, else files_changed/none. `ToolHealth` is plainly `{indexer: Option<String>, last_publish_ms: u64, consecutive_failures: i64, statement_cache_entries: usize}` with no derives (the serialising crate owns serde attributes); `last_publish_ms = latest_generation().duration_ms` and `statement_cache_entries = sangkar_store::db::statement_cache_stats().size` because `&dyn GraphReader` carries no cache member (`SqliteReader::cache_stats` is unreachable through the trait) — deviation reported. Verify: `cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p sangkar-domain --test diff_freshness` exit 0, 7 passed / 0 failed (the_change_set_reports_modified_added_deleted_renamed_and_untracked, a_directory_git_cannot_read_degrades_to_the_digest_comparison, head_commit_of_reads_every_head_shape_and_missing_git_is_none, a_generation_from_another_commit_is_stale_and_the_served_commit_is_fresh, a_busy_indexer_stalls_only_after_the_threshold, a_recorded_root_that_differs_from_the_callers_root_is_the_first_check, health_reports_the_indexer_the_publish_duration_and_the_cache_entries); `cargo test -p sangkar-domain --lib` 9 passed including diff::tests::{sha256_matches_the_published_vectors, name_status_records_split_on_nul_and_keep_the_rename_source, status_records_take_untracked_paths_and_apply_the_prefix} and freshness::tests::{iso8601_round_trips_through_the_parser, the_parser_accepts_the_wire_form_and_refuses_the_rest}; `cargo clippy -p sangkar-domain --all-targets -- -D warnings` exit 0; `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` on the three files exit 0; `cargo test --workspace` 374 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored; `cargo test -p sangkar-boundary` exit 0. Deviations beyond the contract: `Freshness` carries `files_changed_since: usize` (the TS field `status` renders in its summary, so omitting it would force a second hash pass), `FreshnessOptions` carries `repo_root` so root_mismatch is producible, `statement_cache_entries` is the store's process-wide sum, and `sha256_hex` is public so a fixture/indexer computes digests the same way; malformed `-z` records are skipped with no `unmatched` entry because a malformed record carries no path, while a valid-but-unattributable path is recorded there.

Correction to the line counts above: `wc -l` after the last rustfmt pass reports diff.rs 1106, freshness.rs 621, tests/diff_freshness.rs 695 (the preceding entry said 1108 for diff.rs). Everything else in that entry stands; the verify command was re-run after the final edit and is the output quoted there (7 passed, 0 failed).

Orchestrator verification (independent runs): `cargo test -p sangkar-domain --test diff_freshness` -> 7 passed, 0 failed, exit 0, plus 9 lib unit tests; the workspace is 374 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored, clippy and rustfmt clean. Both Done-when clauses are real: `the_change_set_reports_modified_added_deleted_renamed_and_untracked` asserts the rename is ONE entry `("new_name.rs", Renamed, Some("old_name.rs"))` with the old path not left behind as an extra entry ("a rename is ONE entry carrying both paths; a deletion is a state, not an absence"), and then pins `entries.len() == changed.len() + removed.len()` so the two path lists and the entries cannot drift; `head_commit_of_reads_every_head_shape_and_missing_git_is_none` walks a raw-sha detached HEAD, a `ref:` line, a packed refs file and a directory with no `.git`, and skips with a printed message when `git` is absent instead of failing. `STALE_REASONS` is the TypeScript's five-element list verbatim ("none", "files_changed", "root_mismatch", "base_commit_moved", "watcher_stalled"), and I read the git runner: `--no-pager --no-optional-locks -c credential.helper= -c core.askpass=` is present with the reason commented, because a user's git config must not be able to hang the binary on a credential prompt or a pager. tasks.title: Reader goldens: dump the TypeScript answers, compare the Rust ones

details.goal: Prove the Rust reader answers the same rows as the TypeScript reader on the same database, method by method, before any handler depends on it.
details.contract:
`scripts/parity/capture-reader-dump.ts` runs under bun against a fixture indexed by the TypeScript binary and writes `rust/tests/golden/reader/<fixture>.json`, one key per reader method with a deterministic projection:
`find_by_name("<a name that exists twice>")`, `find_by_qn("<qn>")`, `members(<class id>)`, `nodes_by_file(<file id>)`, `inbound`/`outbound` for a node with at least three edges, `metrics_for`, `rows_for_paths(["src"])` and `(["lib"])` on polyglot, `not_indexed_all`, `unresolved_for_files`, `file_by_path`, `all_files`, `census_by_language`, `tests_census`, `meta_for`, `latest_generation`, `removed_symbols_for(<generation>)`, `entry_points(5)`, `hotspots(5)`, `test_gaps(<three ids>)`, `read_node_fts("<a query that matches>", 5)`.
Projections must be stable across runs: ids included (they are rowids and must match only if the two implementations read the same database — which they do), timestamps excluded, and every list in its query order.
`rust/crates/sangkar-store/tests/reader_golden.rs` opens the same `graph.db` (path from an env var the test reads once, `SANGKAR_FIXTURE_DB`, and skipped with a clear message when unset), produces the identical projection through the Rust `GraphReader`, and compares it to the committed JSON with a structural diff that names the method and the first differing element.
Capture for both `polyglot` and `broken`. Do not hand-edit the goldens.
steps: Write the capture script with one deterministic projection per method.
Index both fixtures with the TypeScript binary and write the two golden files.
Write the Rust projection and the comparison test.
Run both and fix any reader mismatch by fixing the Rust query ordering/joins — never by relaxing the comparison.
Commit the goldens and document the `SANGKAR_FIXTURE_DB` contract in the test header.
details.verify:
`~/.bun/bin/bun run scripts/parity/capture-reader-dump.ts` exits 0 and writes two files under `rust/tests/golden/reader/`.
`SANGKAR_FIXTURE_DB=<path to a polyglot graph.db> cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p sangkar-store --test reader_golden` exits 0 and reports 22 compared methods.
Done when: the comparison covers all 22 methods and a deliberately re-sorted `find_by_name` ordering makes it fail.

progress.detail: Projection: both sides emit the same canonical text via a hand-rolled writer (compact JSON, declared key order, null fields omitted, lists in query order, snake_case row names) and the Rust test diffs it structurally, naming method + first differing element path; no serde_json, no numeric-field re-rounding. Excluded: timestamps (published_at/duration_ms), random generation ids (projected as @current/@previous relative to latest_generation()), and machine facts (meta.project_root/branch/remote). Databases: indexed with the TS binary into target/parity-reader-db/<fixture>/graph.db from archives outside git (tmpdir), each published twice (full, then fast after deleting src/duplicate.ts / src/entry.ts) so removed_symbols_for reads 3 / 2 real tombstones; the script prints SANGKAR_FIXTURE_DB=<abs path> cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p sangkar-store --test reader_golden -- --nocapture once per fixture, and the test opens that file read-only (copies to a temp dir first only if a -wal sibling exists) and picks its golden by the fixture label matched against meta.project_name, never the path. Non-empty on polyglot: 19 of 22 (all_files 14, nodes_by_file 10, census 12, find_by_name 4, inbound 5, outbound 4, hotspots 5, read_node_fts 5, unresolved 3, tombstone 3, tests_census 3); empty there: not_indexed_all (fixture has no skips), entry_points (indexer never writes is_entry=1), rows_for_paths("lib") (absent prefix by design); bite-sized empty on broken: inbound, unresolved_for_files, tests_census 0/[], find_by_name 1 row (no duplicate name in that fixture). Deliberate re-sort: BY_NAME_ORDER changed to " ORDER BY n.qn DESC" made the test fail with "find_by_name: the reader and the golden disagree / first difference at find_by_name[0].id: the golden has 92 and the reader answered 95"; nodes.rs restored and verified byte-identical to the pre-edit backup (sha256 cc7b9b71…e69a5c, cmp clean). Verify: capture exits 0 and writes exactly two goldens, recapture is byte-identical; polyglot and broken golden tests both exit 0 and print "22 compared methods"; cargo fmt --check clean, clippy -D warnings clean, cargo test --workspace 375 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored. No divergence was found — the bm25 scores match bit-for-bit (projected as f64 bits).

Orchestrator verification (independent runs): `~/.bun/bin/bun run scripts/parity/capture-reader-dump.ts` exit 0, writes `rust/tests/golden/reader/{polyglot,broken}.json` (16.7 KB / 5.2 KB) and prints one reproduction command per fixture pointing at `target/parity-reader-db/<fixture>/graph.db` (200 KB / 172 KB, gitignored). `SANGKAR_FIXTURE_DB=<polyglot db> cargo test -p sangkar-store --test reader_golden` -> 1 passed, "22 compared methods against the polyglot golden"; the same for broken -> 1 passed, 22 methods. With the variable unset the test passes through an explicit, printed skip that names the capture script and says the goldens are committed while the databases are not — so an unconfigured run can never be mistaken for a green comparison. I re-ran the Done-when's deliberate re-sort myself: changing `BY_NAME_ORDER` from `ORDER BY n.qn` to `ORDER BY n.qn DESC` in `read/nodes.rs` made the test FAIL with "find_by_name: the reader and the golden disagree / first difference at find_by_name[0].id: the golden has 92 and the reader answered 95" — a named method and a named element, exactly as contracted — and restoring the backup returned it to green with `cmp` confirming the file byte-identical to its pre-experiment state. Nine of the twenty-two projections are non-vacuous only on one fixture and the worker listed them rather than presenting a uniform 22/22: on polyglot `not_indexed_all` is 0 (that fixture has no skips, by design) and `rows_for_paths("lib")` is 0 (absent prefix); on broken `inbound`, `unresolved_for_files` and `tests_census` are empty and `find_by_name` returns a single row (no duplicate name there). `removed_symbols_for` is NOT vacuous: the capture indexes each fixture twice, deletes `src/duplicate.ts` / `src/entry.ts` between runs, and compares 3 real tombstones on polyglot and 2 on broken. PRODUCT FACT discovered while checking that, which later phases inherit rather than fix: `entry_points` is empty on BOTH fixtures because `node_metrics.is_entry` is never written by the TypeScript indexer — `grep -rn is_entry src/` finds it only READ (`reader.ts:485`, `metrics.ts`) and DEFAULTED to 0 in `schema.ts:179` — so the entry-point driver in `summary`/`impact` is always 0 on any real graph. Both implementations agree, so parity holds; this is a pre-existing product gap, not a porting defect, and it should not be "fixed" silently inside the migration. No divergence in the first run: all 22 projections matched, including `bm25` scores compared as exact f64 bits (the reason the projection is a canonical string both sides build by hand rather than a JSON round trip, since `sangkar-store` has no `serde_json`). Tests: fmt clean, clippy -D warnings clean, workspace 375 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored.
